drug_class: Smoking cessation aid / Nicotinic receptor partial agonist
purpose: Varenicline is a prescription medicine that helps you quit smoking. It reduces your urge to smoke and makes smoking feel less satisfying if you do slip up. Most people use it as part of a quit-smoking plan that may also include counseling or support groups.
how_it_works: Your brain has special receptors that nicotine from cigarettes attaches to, which causes feelings of pleasure and keeps you coming back for more cigarettes. Varenicline attaches to those same receptors, which calms your cravings and eases withdrawal symptoms. At the same time, it blocks nicotine from fully activating those receptors, so if you do smoke, it won't feel as rewarding.
common_side_effects: Nausea is the most common side effect, especially when you first start — taking it with food and a full glass of water really helps. You may also notice unusual or vivid dreams, headache, trouble sleeping, constipation, or gas. These often get better after the first few weeks.
warnings: Some people notice changes in mood, behavior, or thinking while taking this medicine, such as feeling more depressed, anxious, agitated, or having unusual thoughts. Tell your doctor right away if this happens. Use caution if you have kidney problems, as your dose may need to be adjusted. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery until you know how this medicine affects you, since it can cause drowsiness or dizziness. Do not drink too much alcohol while taking it, as some people have had increased intoxication or unusual behavior.
typical_dosing: You usually start varenicline one to two weeks before your quit date. For the first three days you take one 0.5 mg tablet once a day, then for the next four days you take 0.5 mg twice a day. After that first week, you increase to the full dose of 1 mg twice a day — once in the morning and once in the evening. Always take it with food and a full glass of water. A typical course of treatment is 12 weeks, and your doctor may recommend another 12 weeks to help you stay smoke-free.
